channel.title: Acme: W3C Changes
channel.description: Reports on substantive changes in W3C GitHub repositories.

item.title: Draft Audio Working Group Charter Adds Web MIDI 2.0
item.description:
The draft Audio Working Group charter now lists Web MIDI 2.0 as a potential Recommendation-track deliverable alongside the Web Speech API.

Adoption would depend on specification maturity, support from multiple implementers, and group consensus. The addition is a charter proposal, not a commitment to standardize Web MIDI 2.0.

Changes: charter-drafts commit 26378675.

item.title: SHACL Shapes Graphs Can Suggest Their Data Graphs
item.description:
SHACL 1.2 Core now defines sh:dataGraph, allowing a shapes graph to identify one or more data graphs it is intended to validate. Each value must be an IRI.

A processor may use the hint when the caller has not supplied a data graph explicitly. Unlike sh:shapesGraph, owl:imports in a referenced data graph are not followed.

Changes: data-shapes commit a6ed26f7.

item.title: Chinese Layout Requirements Adds Segmentation and Selection Guidance
item.description:
Requirements for Chinese Text Layout now explains why grapheme, word, and selection boundaries in Chinese cannot always be inferred from spaces. A new example shows how the same character sequence can admit different word segmentations.

The guidance discusses dictionary use, linguistic context, mixed-script text, cursor movement, and selection behavior so editing systems do not impose assumptions derived from space-delimited languages.

Changes: clreq commit 08a701fa.

item.title: MathML Schema Work Begins Aligning with MathML 4
item.description:
The MathML schema repository has begun a MathML 4 XSD based on the MathML 3 schema, with updated semantics content, token elements, links, attributes, and length-percentage values.

Related MathML 3 validation now processes foreign attributes laxly rather than skipping them entirely. The MathML 4 schema remains work in progress.

Changes: mathml-schema commit 9439b477; mathml-schema commit f934f55a; mathml-schema commit 97c0c5b5.

item.title: W3C Process No Longer Requires Advisory Committee Meetings In Person
item.description:
The W3C Process has removed the requirement that its twice-yearly Advisory Committee meetings be face-to-face.

The Team must still organize the meetings and appoint their chair, but the Process now permits remote or hybrid formats without treating them as exceptions.

Changes: process commit 1e355016.

item.title: Draft WoT EtherNet/IP Binding Adds Multidimensional Arrays
item.description:
The draft Web of Things EtherNet/IP binding now describes one- to three-dimensional array fields and the byte size of structured values.

Its JSON Schema rejects unsupported combinations such as arrays of BOOL or STRING and requires structured arrays to declare their element size, giving Thing Descriptions clearer validation.

Changes: wot-binding-templates commit 911be4b7.

item.title: OWL-Time Adds a BFO and Common Core Ontologies Alignment
item.description:
OWL-Time now includes an alignment module for Basic Formal Ontology and Common Core Ontologies.

The document maps temporal entities and relations into those upper ontologies, while the alignment axioms move into a separate RDF file so applications can adopt them without changing the core OWL-Time vocabulary.

Changes: sdw-time commit 497ead79.

item.title: DID Resolution Replaces Dereferencing with a Provisional Algorithm
item.description:
The DID Resolution draft has replaced its former at-risk dereferencing algorithm with a shorter provisional design and removed DID URL dereferencing from the HTTP(S) binding.

It also moves contentType into DID resolution metadata, where that field is defined, rather than DID document metadata. The dereferencing design remains provisional.

Changes: did-resolution commit a43a6588; did-resolution commit 61b8e5e8; did-resolution commit 8e096db9.

item.title: YAML-LD Defines Empty and Multi-Document Stream Behavior
item.description:
YAML-LD now defines how streams of zero or more YAML documents expand and convert to RDF, including empty, comments-only, whitespace-only, and null-root documents.

Null documents contribute no expanded nodes, while blank-node identity can remain shared across documents in one stream. New conformance cases cover mixed empty documents, rejected scalar roots, and reverse conversion.

Changes: yaml-ld commit 82fe1d97; yaml-ld commit 49da7ada; yaml-ld commit 4f586e24; yaml-ld commit 9de11b93; yaml-ld commit fafcf7ae.

item.title: RDF Schema Formalizes Vocabulary Registry Governance
item.description:
RDF Schema now defines admission and custodianship rules for the RDF and RDFS vocabulary registries. New terms must come from Recommendation-track specifications and have general RDF utility.

The responsible Working Group handles changes; if none exists, the W3C Team arranges continued custody. Definitions of rdf:HTML and rdf:XMLLiteral also move from informative to normative text.

Changes: rdf-schema commit 476ad2dc; rdf-schema commit 97352555; rdf-schema commit 83401dd5.

item.title: Turtle and TriG Reserve Version Directives for Future Syntax
item.description:
Turtle 1.2 and TriG 1.2 now require any future incompatible syntax that reuses their media types to declare a version greater than 1.2.

The rule lets older parsers recognize documents that use unsupported future features instead of misinterpreting them as current syntax.

Changes: rdf-turtle commit 438fcc69; rdf-trig commit 7994a40b.

item.title: Linked Web Storage Defines Missing-Container Creation Errors
item.description:
Linked Web Storage now gives create-resource operations an explicit Target Not Found outcome when the destination container does not exist.

The HTTP binding maps that outcome to 404 and no longer phrases the requirement as a broad “MUST return 404 unless” rule, making room for authorization and other failures to take precedence.

Changes: lws-protocol commit 181ed0dc.

item.title: Draft Intentional Friction Note Expands Its Games Analysis
item.description:
The draft Intentional Friction Note now expands its discussion of flow, neurodiversity, information discovery, and high-difficulty “soulslike” games.

It distinguishes challenge that supports a game’s purpose from barriers that merely exclude players, while continuing to flag unresolved sections and editorial work. The document remains an early draft.

Changes: intentional-friction commit 424864ea; intentional-friction commit 9e26ac6e; intentional-friction commit 3b5f82a1; intentional-friction commit 60b530c1.

item.title: WAI Pages Print the Contents of Disclosure Widgets
item.description:
W3C’s accessibility-site theme now expands details elements when printing, so content hidden behind disclosure widgets is not omitted from paper or PDF output.

The print stylesheet also removes the interactive disclosure marker, leaving a clean, complete document.

Changes: wai-website-theme commit fbcd04af.

item.title: WAI Expands Its WCAG Translation Workflow
item.description:
W3C’s guidance for translating WCAG now lays out an eight-step workflow covering source acquisition, translation, previews, checks, issue handling, and final delivery.

It adds clearer repository commands, distinguishes authorized and unofficial translations, and explains how translators should handle markup, links, and generated HTML.

Changes: wai-website commit 03e81b16.

item.title: CSS Kerning Defines Its Dependency on Proportional Alternates
item.description:
CSS Fonts Level 4 now specifies how kerning interacts with CJK fonts whose glyphs become proportionally spaced through the OpenType palt feature.

When palt is active, auto and normal kerning must enable kern; when palt is inactive on fixed-width glyphs, applying kerning is an error. The revision adds examples illustrating the distinction.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit a1dd3973.

item.title: CSS Browser Display Mode Can Match Inside Applications
item.description:
Media Queries Level 5 now says the browser display-mode value matches whenever a browser-style window with normal controls is actually in use.

That can include an application context, allowing browser and application to match concurrently rather than treating browser mode as exclusive to ordinary tabs.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit bfd43540.

item.title: SPARQL CSV Results Clarifies Lossy RDF-Term Serialization
item.description:
The SPARQL CSV results format now explicitly says that IRIs are serialized as their characters and literals as lexical values alone.

Language tags, base direction, and datatype information are omitted, with escaping supplied only by CSV. The wording makes the format’s intentional loss of RDF term metadata unambiguous.

Changes: sparql-results-csv-tsv commit c86791fd.

item.title: Verifiable Credential Confidence Draft Refines Assurance Levels
item.description:
The Verifiable Credential Confidence Method draft now describes assurance levels as scheme-specific ordered values rather than universal scores.

It updates examples and references for NIST and eIDAS, clarifying that issuers must identify the governing framework and that levels from different frameworks are not directly interchangeable.

Changes: vc-confidence-method commit 8c77d0ca.

item.title: Community Group Drafts Gain Clearer Incubation Warnings
item.description:
W3C’s beta Community Group specification design now displays a standard incubation notice and distinct warnings for snapshots, transferred work, and unmaintained documents.

The notice is collapsed and dismissible by default, while transferred specifications direct readers to current contact information. The beta assets also improve link styling and document validation.

Changes: cg-assets commit 351b803f; cg-assets commit d2cf4999; cg-assets commit d4697855.

item.title: Draft WoT Binding Adds Siemens S7Comm
item.description:
A new draft binding maps Web of Things affordances to Siemens S7Comm addressing and operations.

It defines protocol vocabulary, forms, areas, data types, byte and bit offsets, polling, read/write behavior, security considerations, examples, and a JSON Schema. The work is an Editor’s Draft.

Changes: wot-binding-templates commit 206241ca.

item.title: EPUB 3.4 Matches Container Resources Without URL Fragments
item.description:
EPUB 3.4 now requires relative URLs in an OCF container to match an existing resource’s content URL while excluding the fragment component.

The correction distinguishes URL records from source strings and prevents a fragment identifier from making an otherwise valid packaged-resource reference appear missing.

Changes: epub-specs commit bb9ae6f3.

item.title: Web Crypto Updates HMAC to NIST SP 800-224
item.description:
The Web Cryptography specification now references NIST SP 800-224 for HMAC instead of the withdrawn FIPS 198-1 publication.

It also states the hash block sizes used when deriving default HMAC key lengths, including a 512-bit block size for SHA-1 and SHA-256 and a 1024-bit block size for SHA-384 and SHA-512.

Changes: webcrypto commit 84ce2012; webcrypto commit b58e8383; webcrypto commit 893091b5; webcrypto commit 57a2369b.

item.title: Unified Care Model Receives a W3C Namespace
item.description:
W3C’s namespace repository now hosts the Unified Care Model vocabulary at w3.org/ns/ucm.

The namespace document and JSON-LD context identify it as Community Group incubation rather than a W3C standard and define terms for the group’s care-model work.

Changes: ns commit ce359b43.

item.title: Web Crypto Corrects Ed25519 and X25519 Key Mappings
item.description:
The Web Cryptography specification has corrected its SubjectPublicKeyInfo mapping for Ed25519 and X25519.

The algorithm-specific field contains raw public-key bytes rather than another ASN.1 BIT STRING wrapper, aligning the table with the key formats defined for those algorithms.

Changes: webcrypto commit b00c6df2.

item.title: SHACL Node Expressions Expand Conformance Coverage
item.description:
The SHACL 1.2 Node Expressions suite now covers constraints, named and list parameters, ordering, filtering, aggregation helpers, paths, random and time functions, and declared failures.

The draft also refines function-error handling so errors propagate consistently through composed expressions instead of being silently treated as empty results.

Changes: data-shapes commit c1e3f24f.

item.title: MathML 4 Adds Guidance for Accent Characters
item.description:
MathML 4 now discusses the look-alike spacing and combining characters authors may use as mathematical accents.

The guidance points to MathML Core’s supported accent set, notes that only some fonts provide proper stretching and placement, and explains when spacing and non-spacing forms should behave equivalently.

Changes: mathml commit e726b022.

item.title: MathML Intent References Stay Inside the MathML Namespace
item.description:
MathML 4’s intent grammar now limits arg-name lookup to descendant elements in the MathML namespace.

The restriction prevents embedded foreign markup from accidentally satisfying semantic references intended for the mathematical expression.

Changes: mathml commit 6ff48848.

item.title: Verifiable Credentials Starts a Version 2.1 Vocabulary
item.description:
The Verifiable Credentials Data Model repository now contains the first version of a 2.1 credentials vocabulary, separated from the existing 2.0 vocabulary.

Dedicated linting and publication workflows build the new YAML vocabulary, JSON-LD context, diagrams, and human-readable documentation. This is initial 2.1 draft work.

Changes: vc-data-model commit 8838afd0.

item.title: SHACL Stabilizes Variable Pre-Binding and Its Test Suite
item.description:
SHACL-SPARQL has removed the “at risk” marker from its definition of variable pre-binding.

The companion test work retains the approved SHACL 1.2 cases for scope, subqueries, OPTIONAL, UNION, EXISTS, aggregates, paths, and validator parameters while separating unapproved proposals.

Changes: data-shapes commit 6deac327; data-shapes commit 92c22b62.

item.title: CSS Adds flow-start and flow-end Alignment Aliases
item.description:
CSS Box Alignment now defines flow-start and flow-end keywords that follow the container’s layout flow rather than the subject’s own writing mode.

The aliases are incorporated into alignment grammar and Grid masonry examples, giving layouts a way to name the direction in which items are placed without overloading start and end.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 3110cd02.

item.title: SPARQL Rules Adds Grouping and Aggregate Execution
item.description:
The developing SPARQL Rules language now defines GROUP plus COUNT, MIN, MAX, and SUM.

Aggregation rules run once over complete groups after contributing rules have stabilized. New well-formedness and stratification rules prevent order-dependent results and cycles through aggregate dependencies.

Changes: data-shapes commit fcf22c9e; data-shapes commit 26cb8ec8; data-shapes commit e40ae54a.

item.title: Scribe Tool Converts ASCII Dashes During Emphasis Processing
item.description:
W3C’s Scribe meeting-minutes tool now converts double and triple hyphens to en and em dashes when its emphasis-processing option is enabled.

The documented transformation joins its existing substitutions for arrows and emoticons while avoiding longer runs of hyphens.

Changes: scribe2 commit f18cea4b.

item.title: SOSA Aligns Input Values with PROV Usage
item.description:
The SOSA/SSN alignment with PROV now declares sosa:hasInputValue as a subproperty of prov:used.

The axiom lets provenance-aware systems treat values consumed by an observation, actuation, or sampling procedure as entities used by the associated activity.

Changes: sdw-sosa-ssn commit 83889ebe.

item.title: CSS Defines Masking Across Fragmented Boxes
item.description:
CSS Masking now explains how clipping and mask reference boxes behave when an element is split across lines, pages, or columns.

The box-decoration-break property decides whether each fragment gets its own reference box or whether the mask is sliced with the combined decoration, bringing masking in line with other fragmented box effects.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 0c7a1a2a.

item.title: CSS alpha() Now Requires an Explicit Alpha Value
item.description:
CSS Color Level 5 has tightened alpha() syntax: the function now requires an origin color and an explicit alpha value after the slash.

The optional form produced no useful transformation and created parsing ambiguity; authors must now state the channel value or none.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit b186fae2.

item.title: Selectors Level 5 Defines Class-Prefix Selector Grammar
item.description:
Selectors Level 5 now gives the proposed class-prefix selector an explicit grammar: a class identifier ending in a hyphen may be followed by an asterisk.

Whitespace is forbidden between its components, and the asterisk cannot be used when the identifier lacks the trailing hyphen. The feature remains draft work.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 37db3e68.

item.title: CSS scroll-axis-lock Propagates from the Root to the Viewport
item.description:
CSS Overflow Level 5 now says that scroll-axis-lock on the document root applies to the viewport.

Unlike overflow, a value on the HTML body element does not propagate. The clarification removes ambiguity about where authors must set viewport-level axis locking.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit 0ec00ef7.

item.title: SVG 2 Closes use Shadow Trees and Removes an Unimplemented Interface
item.description:
SVG 2 now defines the shadow tree created by a use element as closed. Scripts cannot obtain that tree through a shadowRoot attribute.

The draft consequently removes SVGUseElementShadowRoot, an interface no browser implemented and that no longer has a script-visible object to represent.

Changes: svgwg commit f846f12e; svgwg commit 8c573786.

item.title: SHACL Rules Clarifies Ordering and Immutable Inputs
item.description:
SHACL 1.2 now defines sh:order within a rule layer: lower values run first, same-order rules behave as a group, and inferred triples become visible to later groups in the iteration.

The execution model also states that base and shapes graphs are immutable. Rule additions and deletions affect only the inference graph.

Changes: data-shapes commit 7ff47e1b; data-shapes commit c6357c1a.

item.title: Incremental Font Transfer Recommends Dedicated WOFF2 Flavors
item.description:
The Incremental Font Transfer specification now recommends IFT-specific sfnt flavors when an incremental font is encoded as WOFF2.

Clients convert those flavor tags back to the conventional TrueType or OpenType values after extension. Dedicated tags prevent generic WOFF2 tools from treating incremental fonts as ordinary complete fonts.

Changes: IFT commit 8d778e87.

item.title: DID Resolution Test Suite Adds Missing Core Coverage
item.description:
The DID Resolution interoperability suite now tests the specification’s core resolution section, improves failure diagnostics, and fixes resolver selection and request caching.

Its interoperability report is also configured for publication as a W3C Group Note. The suite removes obsolete dereferencing cases to follow the revised draft.

Changes: did-resolution-test-suite commit b982d58c; did-resolution-test-suite commit 41da570f; did-resolution-test-suite commit 47148ea4; did-resolution-test-suite commit 1e9cc763; did-resolution-test-suite commit 106d8264.

item.title: CSS Lab Conversion Code Preserves Near-Black Precision
item.description:
CSS Color Level 4’s sample Lab-to-XYZ conversion code now rearranges calculations to avoid losing precision near black when implementations use floating-point storage.

The revised formula keeps lightness separate from the added constant and reduces cancellation errors in the low-lightness branch.

Changes: csswg-drafts commit aad431f9.

item.title: SHACL UI Refines Complex Property-Path Editing
item.description:
The SHACL UI draft now distinguishes inverse paths from other complex property paths when describing renderer support.

View mode should support sequence, alternative, repetition, and inverse paths where practical, while edit mode may limit complex paths when a faithful editing interface cannot preserve their meaning.

Changes: data-shapes commit 2f344b97.

item.title: Draft Linked Web Storage Charter Explains Its Predecessors
item.description:
The draft Linked Web Storage Working Group charter now describes its relationship to Linked Data Platform, Solid Protocol, and Fedora API.

It says implementation experience with those systems informs LWS, while departures aim to simplify adoption and improve interoperability through widely deployed standards such as OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect.

Changes: lws-wg-charter commit 6d694e73.

item.title: EPUB Reading-System Tests Expand Japanese Emphasis Coverage
item.description:
W3C’s internationalization suite now packages EPUB tests for emphasis marks under horizontal Japanese text and to the left of vertical text.

Automated tooling builds and validates the EPUB fixtures and their results registry, while committed test books let reading-system implementers run the cases directly.

Changes: i18n-tests commit af50f5cb.

item.title: Long Animation Frames Tightens Timing and Privacy Semantics
item.description:
The Long Animation Frames draft now registers its entry type with Performance Timeline and fixes duration, first-event, paint, promise-invoker, and detached-window handling.

Classic scripts expose the originally requested URL rather than a cross-origin redirect target, call-site locations are defined more precisely, and hidden documents no longer record or report long-animation-frame entries.

Changes: long-animation-frames commit c004dc65; long-animation-frames commit 6e5d150e; long-animation-frames commit 6c5db257; long-animation-frames commit 0a2c6255; long-animation-frames commit 7e91d5c5.

item.title: SHACL UI Adds Semantic Roles for Display Properties
item.description:
The SHACL UI draft now defines property roles for labels, depictions, descriptions, icons, and classifications.

Renderers can use those annotations to choose a resource’s display name, representative image, explanatory text, icon, or type-like classification instead of presenting every property identically.

Changes: data-shapes commit 320dbad2.

item.title: Draft Private Advertising Technology Charter Is Published
item.description:
A draft charter proposes a Private Advertising Technology Working Group to develop interoperable advertising mechanisms with privacy protections.

The document describes proposed scope, deliverables, security and privacy review, coordination, participation, and success criteria. It remains a draft charter and does not itself create the group.

Changes: charter-drafts commit 84018f48.

item.title: WebCodecs Defines Presentation Timestamps
item.description:
WebCodecs now defines a presentation timestamp as an integer number of microseconds describing when frames or chunks should be rendered relative to others in the same media sequence.

The timestamp’s origin belongs to the media producer, not necessarily wall-clock time, and different tracks need not share an origin. Relative deltas preserve capture or playback timing.

Changes: webcodecs commit e68317fd.
